facts.label: reported
facts.quote: August 2012 - Supreme Court directed Sahara India Real Estate Corporation Ltd. (SIRECL) and the Sahara Housing Investment Corporation Ltd. (SHICL) to refund over Rs. 24,400 crore to its investors.
facts.text: In August 2012, the Supreme Court of India ordered two Sahara entities to refund more than 24,400 crore INR collected from public investors through optionally fully convertible debentures.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: during hearing, it was submitted by these societies that an amount of Rs. 86,673 crores has been collected from around 9.88 crore investors and out of which Rs. 62,643 Crore has been invested in Aamby Valley Ltd only.
facts.text: Submissions made before the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies revealed that four Sahara cooperative societies collected 86,673 crore INR from approximately 9.88 crore depositors, funnelling 62,643 crore INR into Aamby Valley Ltd alone.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Out of the total amount of Rs. 24,979.67 Crores lying in the “Sahara-SEBI Refund Account”, Rs. 5000 Crores be transferred to the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies, who, in turn, shall disburse the same against the legitimate dues of the depositors of the Sahara Group of Cooperative Societies, which shall be paid to the genuine depositors in the most transparent manner and on proper identification and on submitting proof of their deposits and proof of their claims and to be deposited in their respective bank accounts directly.
facts.text: The Supreme Court directed that 5,000 crore INR be allocated from the 24,979.67 crore INR lying in the Sahara-SEBI Refund Account to the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies to disburse genuine depositor claims directly to their bank accounts.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Till date, a total amount of Rs 9,267 crore has been refunded to 41,56,711 depositors directly into their Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts.
facts.text: Through the digital CRCS-Sahara Refund Portal, a total amount of 9,267 crore INR has been disbursed directly into the Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of 41,56,711 verified depositors.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The group collected around ₹200 to 300 billion (US$4–6 billion) from over 1.7 million depositors before it collapsed in April 2013.
facts.text: Before unraveling in April 2013, the Saradha Group mobilized an estimated 200 to 300 billion INR from over 1.7 million depositors across Eastern India.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Between 25 and 40% of the deposit was returned to these agents as commissions and lucrative gifts to quickly build up a wide agent pyramid.
facts.text: Saradha expanded its network by returning up to 40% of collected deposit capital to agents in commissions and lavish incentives to assemble a massive recruitment pyramid.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Around 1.74 million depositors filed claims with the commission, of which 83% invested ₹10,000 (US$110) or less.
facts.text: Reflecting the severe exposure of low-income household savings, 83% of the 1.74 million claimants who approached the inquiry commission had deposited 10,000 INR or less.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Presently, each depositor in a bank is insured upto a maximum of ₹ 5,00,000 /- (Rupees Five Lakhs only) for both principal and interest amount held by him/her in the “same right and same capacity” as on · the date of liquidation/cancellation of a bank's licence
facts.text: Unlike unregulated collective schemes and primary societies, bank deposits in insured commercial and cooperative banks carry mandatory statutory coverage from the DICGC up to a ceiling of 500,000 INR per depositor.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: As informed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), 978 cases of unauthorized collection of funds were discussed in State Level Coordination Committee (SLCC) Meetings in various States/ UTs and were given to the respective regulators/ law enforcement agencies in the States for dealing with the complaints.
facts.text: To crack down on unlicensed deposit collections across states, 978 cases of unauthorized fund raising were flagged and reviewed in State Level Coordination Committee meetings convened by regulators and state enforcement bodies.

intro.prompt: 9:16 vertical, 1080x1920, about 8 seconds, photorealistic and cinematic, bright vivid colour. Setting: wide shot of a crowd of anxious small-town Indian depositors, elderly men in kurtas and women in sarees, holding old passbooks outside a locked, rusted metal shutter of a small deposit office, late afternoon dusty light. The background is real and in motion behind him (as fits the place: waves, mist, leaves, flags, lamps flickering, people walking, traffic, light shifting); never a still, flat or heavily blurred backdrop. Framing: medium shot from the waist up, his whole head and both shoulders inside the frame with clear space above his hair and on both sides, and he stays framed like this to the end; do not crop the top of his head. Lighting: warm key light on the face, a soft rim light on the hair, matched to the scene; flattering, no harsh shadows, no dull or flat grey look. SG [locked] standing relaxed and upright, shoulders open, wearing a maroon blazer over a black tee. Speaks from the first frame, mouth matched to the words, steady eye contact with the lens. Face and delivery: a confident, charismatic documentary presenter. Calm, natural face with a pleasant, warm smile, relaxed eyebrows, eyes soft and focused on the viewer. On "phir paisa kyun atka" the eyes narrow a little with intrigue and the head tilts slightly, as if sharing a secret. On "Ruko, asli khel baaki!" a warm, confident smile and one small nod. Natural blinking, subtle head movement. No exaggerated expressions: no wide eyes, no raised eyebrows, no open-mouth surprise, no big grin, no frown; never sad, gloomy, worried or tired. Voice: warm, clear, measured, with quiet intensity; a short pause before "phir paisa kyun atka". Hands: one slow, small gesture toward the scene behind him on the first line, then hands rest; no fast or large arm movements. Camera: eye level, a very slight slow push-in, slight handheld feel. Empty hands, no prop. @SGLearning watermark in the top right corner, white, bold, 80% opacity. No captions, no subtitles, no other on-screen text. No hologram, no floating screen, no graph, no chart, no laptop, tablet, monitor, TV or glowing blue panel anywhere in the frame. Export at 1080x1920.
